subject: Materials Science
title: Why Ceramics Hate Tension
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Ceramics Hate Tension usable.

hook.text: Stand on a ceramic tile and it holds. Pull it apart and it snaps instantly.

buildup.text: Ceramics are strong in compression — atoms push together and the bonds hold firm.

discovery.text: In tension, tiny surface flaws concentrate stress and grow into cracks instantly.

twist.text: A scratch invisible to the eye can cut a ceramic's tensile strength by 90 percent.

climax.text: That's why ceramic columns work perfectly — they carry loads in pure compression.

punchline.text: Squeeze a ceramic and it's a hero. Pull it and it's a coward.

quiz.question: Why do ceramics fail easily in tension?
options: Surface flaws concentrate stress and propagate as cracks
